F1 gives the device entry a documentation link and a real manufacturer, neither of which exists today; F2 gives the repair notices a documentation link they currently all lack. CARRIED FROM #540 (#524/#525): _shutdown_process_pool must NOT be called inline from a coroutine -- it is reaped at EVENT_HOMEASSISTANT_STOP on the executor, and the atexit backstop is left with nothing to wait for. Home Assistant's own loop-protection helper (upstream, not in this tree) compares the calling thread id against the loop's; time.sleep is protected and Popen.wait is not, but CPython's Popen._wait polls with time.sleep, which is why the detector fires. A coverage test that calls the reaper directly from async context will trip it. Also: tests/nightly_ha.py's KNOWN_BLOCKING now lists two offenders this fix removed, and Checks.check BLANKS the detail on pass, so the stale pin is SILENT -- a regression of either would pass the nightly (#533).
